zones._how: Photo 032 (= the owner's 0387927a, mean pixel difference 1.2 of 255) was taken from the crane parked at the NW end. A level-camera perspective fit of the nine visible columns of the left row (6 m pitch) gives rms 3.0 px, vanishing point u 624, horizon v 262 (from the runway girders), f*h 3821 px*m from two column bases, camera 6.88 m up (VGGT: 7.33), 1.7 m left of the nave axis, 3.8 m in front of the entry grid line (first visible column 14.2 m ahead = grid line s 18; VGGT puts the end wall 1-4 m behind the camera). Each marked pixel is put on the floor: D = f*h/(v - 262), lateral = (u - 624)*h/(v - 262). Cross-check: the ground photos 018-025, taken beside the press, sit 39-46 m from the crane camera in the VGGT cloud (the fit puts the press base 47 m out). Bay count in photo 032: the dance floor spans bays 1-5 from the crane, the stage front is at grid line 5 (s 30), the press stands at grid line 9 (s ~51-54), beside the expansion joint (paired columns, photo 021 taken there).

photo-032.note: hall frame. Fitted on the photo (level camera, horizon v 262, vanishing point u 624, f 555 px): yaw = atan((640-624)/555) to the right, and the off-centre horizon rendered as a 10 deg pitch down — the photo itself is level with its principal point off-centre, so a render's verticals converge slightly where the photo's do not.

photo-024.note: REFIT 2026-09-28 (hall fix): OpenCV solvePnP (SQPnP then iterative LM) on 6 picked points — the nave lantern's near and far deck-opening corners (x ±6, y 13.7, z -7.25 / -45.75) and the far gate's top corners (x ±2.4, y 5.4, z -54.5) — with the EXIF intrinsics (f 1498 px, centred principal point, no distortion term). rms 37 px on 2992 (was ~90 px from the 5-point fixed-height fit). Height came out 1.0 m (VGGT 1.54): a low hand or the ultra-wide's uncorrected distortion; roll ~ -6 deg is not modelled by the renderer's camera. Script: session scratchpad hallfix/fit024.py. Still APPROXIMATE: good to ~1 m and ~2 deg.

dimsSource: photographs: VGGT (Wang et al., CVPR 2025), weights facebook/VGGT-1B @ 860abec7 (CC BY-NC 4.0); photographs (perspective fit on photo 032) and the owner's marks; unstated; photographs: see file; aerial survey (two Esri/Maxar captures 2020 and 2024, OSM, Microsoft ML footprints) and photo 007 crane metrology; read off pictures, not taped

notes: Roof: a flat steel double-layer space frame (square-on-square offset grid of pyramids, star gusset nodes, corrugated deck on the top chords), photos 017, 020, 021, 023, 024, 034, 035. Bottom chord 11.0 m, top chord 13.5 m. It is NOT the 'Kislovodsk' (TsNIISK) series, which is 3 x 3 m at 2.12 m depth for low buildings (corrected 2026-10-02): the family is unidentified.

Lanterns: raised flat-top box lanterns 12 m wide, ~3.5 m above the deck, over spans 2 and 3 only, each line split in two ~38.5 m segments with a ~14.5 m gap at the expansion joint (Esri Wayback 37890, Maxar WV-3 2020-10-30). The satellite put the gap centre at v = -2 m from the roof centre; the roof edge and the 108 m grid disagree by 1.5 m, so the joint is taken on the grid centre line (paired columns, Soviet practice: each 500 mm off the line) and the segments are centred on it: setback 8.25 m from the end grid lines (satellite 7-8.5).

Columns: precast concrete, a solid lower shaft; at crane level the head flares SYMMETRICALLY across the hall with 45-deg chamfers (Y / goblet), one steel crane girder on each side, a centred upper column to the space frame. Not flared along the row (photo 038).
Crane runway: grey steel plate girders with web stiffeners (photo 004 right), two per inner row, a handrail along the nave-side girder.

Walls: no nave wall, no clerestory, no aisles — the four spans share one flat roof. Outer long walls only at the building edge (concrete panels, 3 ribbon window bands). Low block walls ~3 m in some bays.

Heights and the span/pitch ratio: carried over from moxir-hall-dims-2026-09-27.json (VGGT + perspective); the camera height fitted on photo 032 on 2026-09-28 (6.9 m, see the features file) agrees with VGGT's 7.3 m within 6%.

2026-09-28 hall fix (owner: 'so fix all make it right right'): the space frame is BIG — 6 x 6 m square pyramids 2.5 m deep (the chord planes 11.0/13.5 m, VGGT), star gusset nodes at every bottom node, heavy chords; the lantern keeps its own 3 m frame. v2 drew a thin 3 m lattice everywhere (wrong: the photos' module is the column pitch).

2026-10-02 hall corrections, each with its source: (1) the LEFT low wall is 2 closed bays, not 5 (the 09-28 features file said bays 3-7 from photo 032, wrong): from_door_m [24, 36]. (2) the RIGHT low wall (a GUESS in the 09-28 file, [60, 84]) is deleted: the right row is open (003, 005, 006, 009, 027: machinery and pipes between the columns). (3) the crane cab hangs at the RIGHT (+x) end (002, 003, 004, 005, 009, 013), x 8.35-10.35 in the nave crane's frame. (4) the roof underside 11.0 -> 10.8 m (Soviet height series 8.4 / 9.6 / 10.8 / 12.0) and the top chord 13.5 -> 13.3 (2.5 m depth kept). (5) the lantern 3.5 -> 3.2 m (standard lantern for a 24 m span: 2.77 or 3.22 m). (6) the right runway girder has no handrail; the left one keeps it.

Left unchanged on purpose: the crane rail (7.6 m in this layer set; the standards give 7.75 for 16-20 t or 8.15 for <= 10 t cranes and the crane's capacity is unknown, so measure on site); the 6 x 6 x 2.5 m space frame (photo-derived; it is NOT the 'Kislovodsk' series, which is 3 x 3 x 2.12 m for low buildings); the expansion joint (the lantern gap is the evidence); the floor-rail gauge (unmeasured).

photo-032.note: hall frame. Fitted on the photo (level camera, horizon v 262, vanishing point u 624, f 555 px): yaw = atan((640-624)/555) to the right, and the off-centre horizon rendered as a 10 deg pitch down — the photo itself is level with its principal point off-centre, so a render's verticals converge slightly where the photo's do not.
